transcript:
Meeting: Aurora Systems — inference cost & deployment options discovery
Date: 2025-12-03 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~57 mins
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Eli Navarro (Redwood Solutions); Michael Tanner (Aurora CTO); Leah Ortiz (Aurora VP Product); Samir Patel (Aurora ML Eng); Dana Ruiz (Aurora Infra)

Summary: Quick intro, then deep into cost levers: per-token pricing, batching, KV prefix caching, quantization. Customer is evaluating hosted first vs reserved Dedicated, with Private as a potential requirement for data residency. They have a tight budget window for Q1 and need clear unit-econ numbers to present to finance.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call — Jordan from Redwood, Priya is our SE, Eli on solutions side. Uh, maybe quick intros from Aurora?
[00:15] Michael: Yeah hi I'm Michael, CTO, we've been kicking the tires on a couple LLM vendors, our main thing is cost predictability and low p95 latency, especially for interactive experiences.
[00:22] Leah: Leah here, product, mostly interested in user experience — p50 latency under 200ms if possible but we can trade a bit for cost.
[00:30] Samir: Samir, ML, I'll be running the tests, the model family we're prototyping on is a 30B dense transformer — mostly summarization and Q&A style prompts.
[00:38] Dana: Dana, infra, I'll be focused on networking and security — VPC, peering, and KMS integrations matter for us.
[01:00] Priya: Great — goal for today is to understand your workload and constraints and to outline what a pilot looks like. We'll cover per-token economics and the levers we typically recommend: batching, KV prefix cache, quantization and routing.
[01:18] Michael: Sounds good, we have a very narrow budget for Q1, can you give us rough numbers for hosted vs dedicated?
[01:28] Jordan: Short answer — hosted is easiest to start and the per-token public pricing is competitive, but if you get to sustained high TPS/Duty cycles, Dedicated with committed capacity often reduces unit cost 20-40% depending on batching and quantization.
[01:48] Leah: Can you explain the math — like what's in that 20-40%?
[01:55] Priya: Sure — it's a mix: dedicated gives you amortized GPU time, fewer cold starts, and you can enable more aggressive batching and KV cache pinning. On hosted we still do batching and caching, but you might hit multi-tenant limits for extreme bursty p95 low-latency SLAs. Also, in Dedicated you can apply int8/int4 quant variants which reduce GPU memory and increase spec throughput, lowering cost per token.
[02:30] Samir: For our 30B model, what's a ballpark tokens/sec and p95 numbers we should expect on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[02:38] Priya: Ballpark, on a cabled high-throughput GPU with 30B and int8, steady-state throughput for single-stream with batching could be — p50 around 80-120ms, p95 maybe 200-350ms depending on sequence length. Hosted tiers will be similar median but Dedicated lets you tune batch windows and kernel selection so you can push cost down. These are rough — we'd run a bench.
[03:10] Michael: Bench makes sense. On the cost side, how do you account for system tokens vs user tokens? We're trying to calculate effective price per user-turn.
[03:20] Jordan: We report both raw per-token charges (input/output) and you can instrument token-level breakdowns in Console. Effective unit economics come from reducing total tokens via structured outputs and caching repeated prefixes. Also batching reduces per-token compute overhead.
[03:40] Leah: Can you unpack caching? We have a lot of repeated system prompts and some long prefix contexts.
[03:48] Priya: Absolutely — Redwood supports prefix/KV caching. If you have repeated system prompts or shared context chunks, the KV cache stores attention key/value states so repeated calls reuse cached KV and only compute delta tokens. For many customers that reduced effective compute by 15-50% depending on reuse patterns. Note sometimes transcription shows "KV cash" in our notes but it's KV cache.
[04:30] Samir: Is that automatic on Hosted? Any config?
[04:35] Priya: On Hosted it's available but aggressive pinning and longer TTLs are more configurable on Dedicated. We'll show you TTL and cache key strategies in the benchmark plan.
[04:48] Dana: From infra side — if we go Private, we need KMS / HSM options and to be able to keep logs inside our VPC. How heavy is the on-prem footprint?
[04:58] Eli: Private can be packaged to run within your VPC or on-prem; the control plane can be customer-managed — we integrate with customer KMS, and audit logs can stay on-prem. It is heavier — typically involves more ops work and a longer timeline (6-12 weeks) vs Hosted (days) or Dedicated (2-4 weeks).
[05:22] Michael: We might prefer Hosted to get started but finance will ask if Dedicated will save money at scale. Can you run an example scenario — say 100M tokens/month — show hosted vs dedicated?
[05:32] Jordan: Yeah we'll create a worked example. Quick rule of thumb: hosted baseline price X per 1k tokens. Dedicated effective cost depends on commit size, but for 100M tokens/month with good batching + int8 you could be 25-35% cheaper. We'll put the spreadsheet together.
[06:05] Leah: What about fallbacks — if Dedicated capacity maxes out can we failover to Hosted?
[06:12] Priya: Yes — smart routing policies let you fallback to hosted or a different model family. Redwood's runtime supports automated fallback to compatible variants with minimal service disruption. You'll see some latency increase but it's controlled.
[06:30] Samir: A lot of our prompts are sensitive — what about encryption at rest/in transit and auditability?
[06:36] Eli: By default we do TLS in transit; for Private deployments you can use your KMS and we're SOC2 compliant by default on hosted. For more regulated needs we offer additional controls and audit logs retention options.
[06:55] Michael: Finance will want to know the break-even point for Dedicated. Can you describe the variables that matter most?
[07:00] Priya: Break-even depends on: commit size, average sequence lengths, fraction of repeated prefixes (caching benefit), ability to use quantized models (int8/int4), and acceptable p95 latency SLOs (larger batch windows reduce cost but raise p95). We also consider token composition — embeddings vs generation.
[07:28] Leah: On quantization — does Redwood provide quantized model variants or do we need to fine-tune?
[07:35] Priya: We provide verified quantized variants for many open models and will recommend per-workload whether int8 or int4 is suitable. For some sensitive workloads we recommend evaluating quality degradation with eval sets.
[07:52] Samir: Ok, for the bench, can we test three configs: Hosted default; Dedicated commit with int8; Dedicated commit with int4 + batching?
[07:59] Priya: Yes that's exactly the plan we typically run. We'll capture p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec, and cost per Million tokens as run.
[08:10] Michael: How do we estimate cost for dev vs prod vs peak? We have spiky traffic with short bursts.
[08:16] Jordan: We work with autoscale on Dedicated and burst pools, but Dedicated gives you predictable baseline and you can enable burst-to-hosted for super peak. For spiky traffic you pay for the baseline reserved capacity and transient hosted on top — we'll model that in the sheet.
[08:40] Dana: Network latency matters — what are typical regional considerations? We need EU data residency for some customers.
[08:47] Eli: We have regional endpoints and can deploy Dedicated/Private into EU regions. For Hosted you can pick region and we do data residency controls; Private is obviously local. We'll provide region-specific latency expectations in the bench.
[09:05] Leah: Any gotchas on billing? Like hidden data egress or additional infra charges?
[09:12] Jordan: The hosted per-token includes compute and infra; if you need retained logs beyond standard retention or advanced observability that's an add-on. For Dedicated there can be infra pass-throughs depending on private cloud. We'll highlight all line items.
[09:30] Michael: Security diligence — they'll ask for SOC2 and an architecture diagram. Can you share security pack?
[09:36] Eli: Yes — we'll send SOC2 attestation and our security workbook. For Private we'll also share deployment runbook.
[09:45] Priya: For the benchmark we'll need Samir to share a 48-72 hour traffic sample, including token lengths and percent of repeated prefixes. That helps us model realistic caching gains.
[09:59] Samir: I'll get that over; we'll anonymize PII.
[10:05] Jordan: Great. Quick aside on model routing — if you want lower cost, sometimes we route to a 13B variant for low-stakes requests and keep 30B for high-quality results. That hybrid routing can cut cost substantially.
[10:22] Leah: Do you have examples of real customers that did hybrid routing? Any numbers?
[10:26] Priya: Yes — typical savings vary a lot, but we've seen customers cut cost 30-60% by routing low-complexity queries to smaller models and using caching. We'll anonymize a case study.
[10:43] Michael: Timeline — pilot for Q1: what's realistic?
[10:48] Eli: If you're starting Hosted-only pilot you can start in under a week. For Dedicated with a small commit it's 2-4 weeks to provision and tune; Private is longer and usually targeted for enterprise agreements.
[11:03] Dana: For Private we'd need to schedule a security architecture review — can we do that in parallel?
[11:09] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll parallelize security review with bench prep.
[11:15] [--- long middle section of technical Q&A, timestamps every ~1-2 minutes as we deep dive ---]
[20:10] Samir: On batching — is there a recommended batch target? Our UX needs some sub-200ms interactions, so large batch windows may hurt.
[20:17] Priya: Right — there's a trade: small batch windows (e.g., 10-30ms) keep latency low but reduce batching efficiency. For interactive apps we often aim for adaptive batching that targets a p50 under X ms while letting background workloads use larger windows. We can tune per-route.
[25:35] Michael: Can the console show token-level cost per route? We'd like to attribute cost to product features.
[25:42] Jordan: Yes, Console has per-route breakdowns and you can attach metadata to requests so features are billable units.
[29:50] Leah: Is there a quick way to project 6-month spend if we move from Hosted to Dedicated at month 3?
[29:58] Jordan: We'll model that in the pricing sheet — include commit start date and amortize any setup fees.
[33:00] Priya: Quick note — for some models there are quantization quality trade-offs. We'll run prompt-level evals and show metrics: ROUGE/BLEU or embedding similarity depending on application.
[35:24] Michael: Any legal constraints on sharing model logs with us if Hosted? We need some audit trail but logs may contain PII.
[35:31] Eli: Logs can be redacted and retention policies adjusted. For HIPAA-level needs we often recommend Private and custom ingestion pipelines.
[38:15] Samir: For the bench, can we measure cost per 1M tokens and p95 on 3 sequences lengths: short (<=128 tokens), medium (128-512), long (512-2048)?
[38:24] Priya: Yes — that's the plan. We'll run across those buckets and show caching impact.
[41:10] Leah: One more on KPIs — finance will want a simple metric: $ per active user month — can you approximate?
[41:16] Jordan: We'll show both $ per 1M tokens and example $ per DAU based on your sample traffic — that's in the sheet.
[44:00] Michael: Pricing transparency — can you show exact numbers not a range? We need to present to procurement.
[44:06] Jordan: We'll give committed Dedicated pricing with explicit assumptions and hosted list price. Some discounts are negotiable for annual deals; we'll document everything.
[47:30] Dana: Regarding network setup for Private, how intrusive is the peering? Do you require open ingress?
[47:36] Eli: We do cross-account VPC peering with restricted endpoints; generally we don't need open ingress. We'll share a network diagram.
[50:10] Samir: A small question on quantization tooling — do you provide accuracy tooling for int4 validation?
[50:16] Priya: Yes — we run eval harnesses and can produce a delta quality report per prompt set. We usually recommend customers run a short A/B test in prod-like config.
[52:05] Jordan: Ok we're about out of time — quick recap: Redwood to send pricing worksheet, Priya to send benchmark plan, Samir to share sample traffic, Dana to confirm VPC constraints, and schedule security review.
[52:20] Michael: Sounds good. Any other questions?
[52:25] Leah: No, thanks.
[52:31] Samir: I'll aim to get the sample data by Friday.
[52:37] Jordan: Perfect. We'll follow up with proposed pilot timeline and a calendar invite for security review.
[52:45] [END]

References shared: pricing worksheet (link placeholder), security pack (link placeholder), benchmark plan (to be shared).

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" vs KV cache; "sammel" for SAML).

Call ended with explicit next steps and action items.
